condition: acute severe pediatric upper airway obstruction presenting with continuous loud harsh inspiratory stridor at rest following mild viral rhinorrhea
level_rationale: Continuous loud harsh inspiratory stridor on every breath at rest tonight in a 2-year-old boy following mild watery nasal discharge yesterday indicates moderate-to-severe acute upper airway obstruction requiring immediate emergency hospital evaluation for nebulized epinephrine, systemic corticosteroids, and airway monitoring, whereas giving 3 brief dry coughs after lying down tonight after yesterday's mild watery runny nose describes an uncomplicated mild viral cold appropriate for home supportive self-care.

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (2-year-old son, mild watery runny nose yesterday, and continuous loud harsh inspiratory stridor on every breath at rest tonight) with a 2-word span difference (18 vs 20 words), zero diagnosis labels ('croup' omitted), and 8 shared trailing tokens ('tonight so I need to go to the'). Under Rule A and Rule D, replacing continuous resting stridor in f3 with a positive unprompted mild symptom ('gave 3 brief dry coughs after lying down') keeps the same viral prodrome while shifting care cleanly from emergency hospital evaluation (level 4) to home self-care (level 1) with zero stated negatives.
